SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

8. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

9. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

13. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.

15. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
